messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: max memory for r
messages.body_plain:
This issue appears to depend on the OS and the architecture:
Windows/not_Windows, 32-bit/64-bit.  I can't tell what the OP is
using.

Have a look at:

?memory.limit

Note, in particular:
     On non-Windows platforms these are stubs which report infinity
          (‘Inf’) with a warning.

     A number: On Windows, size in Mb (1048576 bytes), rounded to 0.01
     Mb for ‘memory.size’ and rounded down for ‘memory.limit’.

And for the record, memory is typically reported in bytes, not bits (a
bit is a single binary digit; a byte is an addressable collection of
bits, usually 8 bits these days).

Also for the record: I don't know if there is a standard notation, but
using lower-case 'b' for "bytes" (as in the R help page noted above)
seems confusing to me.  It would make more sense, to me at least,
that, for instance, "MB" should refer to "megabytes", and "Mb" should
refer to "megabits".  (I suppose that the use cases are sufficiently
distinct that there should be no confusion, but...)

messages.subject: Analyst Position
messages.body_plain:
Hello All,
Myself and some collaborators have procured a NFWF grant for some salt marsh harvest mouse research here in the bay, and we have some money to hire an analyst, and I thought some folks on this list might be interested and qualified.  At a baseline we are going to be building some population models and testing environmental correlates, but if we had the right person, it could potentially go a lot further.  The position would essentially be a post-doc type position.  I think the grant controller was trying to run it as an actual post-doc position through UCD, but I think there is also a pretty good chance that they would hire the person outright.  If you are interested, or know someone who might be interested and qualified please let me know.  We aren't super concerned about degrees, we just basically need someone who is better at analysis than I am.  Bonus points for familiarity with the habitats and wildlife of the San Francisco Bay.

Thanks!
🐀
Katie

--
Katherine Smith, PhD
Post-Doctoral Researcher
UC Davis
Department of Wildlife, Fish and Conservation Biology
One Shields Avenue
Davis, CA 95616
(530) 400-7729 (cell)

messages.subject: Invitation to D-RUG aRt night
messages.body_plain:
Come to our second aRt Social!
Working in R? Can’t get any analyses done because you’re too distracted by ideas for gorgeous plots? Sounds like you could use a beer, some snacks and a few dedicated hours to generate beautiful aRtwork to share for a good cause! Join us!
Tuesday, February 25, 530-8pm
508 2nd St, Suite 208, Davis

Hosted by the Davis R-Users Group & Dryad. Bring your laptop, some data from your research to visualize, and your creative pants. We’ll provide beer & refreshments, good tunes, power outlets, and help with R.

We’ll be uploading all the images to our nascent society6 artist page <https://society6.com/davisrusersgroup>. Proceeds from sales will go to a charity fund at The Carpentries to bring workshops to underrepresented regions and groups. Click the link above to see examples from aRt night in 2016.

For some inspiration, take a look at some of these links:
https://github.com/marcusvolz/mathart
https://github.com/will-r-chase/aRt
https://github.com/cutterkom/generativeart
https://ambient.data-imaginist.com/
https://www.data-imaginist.com/art
amazing maps by @hrbrmstr: https://github.com/hrbrmstr/y2019-30daymapchallenge
accidental aRt <https://d-rug.github.io/blog/2016/accidental-art.tumbler.com>

We’re excited to see what we all come up with!
The Fine Print

The images we create will be available to the public as different kinds of art products, so if you don’t want to use your own data, that’s fine! The idea is not so much to share scientific results, but to generate aesthetically pleasing images from data that can be sold for a good cause. If you would like to use your own data but don’t know where to start, we can help you randomize or anonymize a subset that would be appropriate to use to generate abstract images.

messages.subject: Announcing new question forum for D-RUG
messages.subject_clean: Announcing new question forum for D-RUG
messages.body_plain:
Hello All!

We are excited to announce a new resource for our group. We have created a discourse server for Davis R Users Group. This server is similar to StackOverflow in layout and function, but it will allow us to better ask and answer questions as a group. The questions will be better organized and easily searchable, which we think is an improvement over our listserve. We've imported all the previous posts and questions from the Google listserve, they can all be found under the "d-rug archives" category.

We still plan to use the google listserve to announce physical meetups or other logistics, and if you'd like to post there, one of the coordinators will moderate posts before they are sent.

You can see our site here: d-rug.discourse.com <http://d-rug.discourse.com>
We chose to to password protect the group to discourage unfriendly users from drive-by interactions. Anyone is welcome to join the group!

Happy posting :)

Best,
Taylor, Ryan, Martha, and Michael

--
Taylor Reiter
PhD Candidate
Food Science Graduate Group
Lab for Data Intensive Biology
University of California, Davis
